title: collector-pseudonymization-and-field-mapping-spec
content:
Purpose and motivation:
This note proposes a concrete spec for field-level pseudonymization and canonical field mapping inside evidence collectors (edge/host-side) that feed Redwood's evidence ingest pipeline and SIEM exports. Goal: reduce PII/PHI footprint upstream, preserve forensic utility for security ops, and map RBAC-v2 audit fields into a SIEM-friendly canonical schema.

Context and constraints (quick):
- Several collectors currently ship raw user/account identifiers in the audit payloads. We need to provide a stepwise mitigation that: (1) masks or pseudonymizes high-risk identifiers at source, (2) preserves deterministic linkability where needed for incident triage, and (3) emits mapping artifacts to a secure key-service (KMS/HSM-backed) for controlled re-identification in emergencies.
- Collectors operate in environments with different trust boundaries: hosted agents (Redwood-managed), dedicated customer agents (isolated), and private on-prem agents. Spec must be implementable across all three modes with configuration toggles.
- RBAC-v2 introduces new fields (role_id, role_version, effective_permissions) that must be preserved in the canonical audit schema for policy forensics.

Scope:
- Applies to all evidence collectors under security-and-compliance: agent-side log shippers, proof-ingest adapters, and lightweight sidecars that capture control-plane and data-plane audit events.
- Not in scope: downstream SIEM retention policies (but we provide guidance); model for long-term key escrow (separate KMS design).

Definitions (for this doc):
- Pseudonymization: deterministic transformation of an identifier to an irreversible-but-reversible token using a keyed HMAC or AEAD-derived token, where the key is stored in KMS for re-identification under strict access controls.
- Masking: irreversible redaction where re-identification is not possible (e.g. hash truncated without key).
- Canonical field: standardized field name and type used by SIEM/export adapters (see mapping table below).

Design principles:
1) Least-exposure: default outgoing payloads must not include raw user identifiers unless explicitly allowed by policy.
2) Tiered tokenization: allow both deterministic pseudonyms (for triage joins) and masked fields for public/logging endpoints.
3) Auditability: every pseudonymization operation must emit a local audit trace (non-PII) that records which transformation was applied and which KMS key id was used.
4) Configurable policy: collectors must reference a local policy file (YAML) to decide which fields to tokenise vs mask vs keep.
5) Performance-sensitive: pseudonymization implementation should support batched HMACs and optional local crypto caching for throughput-sensitive agents.

High-level flow (collector):
1. Collect event (raw).
2. Normalize fields to canonical names (mapper).
3. Apply field policies (tokenize/mask/keep).
4. Emit pseudonymization audit record to local persistent queue (encrypted) and forward transformed event to ingest pipeline.
5. Where deterministic tokens are produced, optionally emit secure mapping into key service (encrypted channel).

Field mapping table (canonical targets):
(plain text table as reference for implementers)
- source_user_id -> subject.id (string) : Pseudonymize by default. Deterministic tokenization recommended. Store key id used in local audit record.
- source_user_email -> subject.email (string) : Mask domain and local-part per policy (default mask local-part: "u***@example.com"). Optional pseudonymize if allowed.
- account_id -> account.id (string) : Deterministic pseudonymization. Required for multi-tenant forensic joins.
- role_id -> rbac.role_id (string) : Keep (do not pseudonymize). RBAC roles are low risk but required for policy analysis.
- role_version -> rbac.role_version (string) : Keep.
- effective_permissions -> rbac.permissions (array:string) : Keep.
- resource_path -> resource.path (string) : Pseudonymize segments containing user identifiers, keep resource types.
- ip_address -> network.ip (string) : Mask last octet by default (e.g. 10.20.30.xxx); optional full pseudonymization when customer policy requires.
- session_id -> session.id (string) : Pseudonymize but preserve determinism within a 30-day rolling window.
- timestamp -> event.ts (RFC3339) : Keep with ms precision. Emit collector local ingestion timestamp as event.ingested_ts.
- raw_payload -> event.payload (string) : By default, omit: collectors should only attach a payload when a policy flag enables it. When attached, payload must have high-risk fields masked/pseudonymized first.

Pseudonymization algorithm (recommended):
- Deterministic token: token = base58urlencode(HMAC-SHA256(key_id || key_version || field_name || value) [first 18 bytes])
- Keys: use per-environment key wrapping via KMS. Collector MUST NOT store raw unwrapped keys on disk.
- Non-deterministic token (for one-time masking): use AEAD encryption of value with fresh nonce and drop nonce on emit if irreversible masking desired.
- Re-identification: a separate secure utility (rbac-protected) calls KMS unwrap + verifies audit approvals before returning original value.

Operational notes and SLOs:
- Latency: local pseudonymization should add < 3ms per event in normal mode; batching/hmac pipelines should keep end-to-end collector latency < 20ms for single-event paths.
- Throughput: collector should support 2k rps per core in bulk mode; document performance tests included in linked artifacts.
- Local audit queue: limited retention (30d) and encrypted-at-rest; purge policy configurable.

SIEM export mapping and compression guidance:
- SIEM receives canonicalized, tokenized events. Mapped fields (subject.id, account.id, rbac.role_id, event.ts, network.ip) are top-level.
- Avoid embedding raw_payload. If necessary, store payload in encrypted blobstore and include blob reference id in SIEM event.
- Export adapters must tag records with pseudonymization_version and key_id so that downstream analysts can scope re-identification requests.

RBAC-v2 considerations (how to keep forensics intact):
- Do NOT pseudonymize role_id or effective_permissions. These fields are authoritative policy artifacts and do not contain user-identifying data.
- For fields where exposure is required for policy evaluation (e.g., resource owner mapping), prefer deterministic pseudonyms rather than raw ids. This allows SRE/security to reconstruct joins without exposing raw identifiers in logs.

Audit log schema examples (canonicalized event):
{
  "event.ts": "2025-01-10T16:23:12.123Z",
  "event.ingested_ts": "2025-01-10T16:23:12.178Z",
  "subject.id": "tok_b58_1ag9x...",
  "subject.email": "u***@example.com",
  "account.id": "tok_b58_9xmx2...",
  "rbac.role_id": "billing-admin",
  "rbac.role_version": "v2",
  "rbac.permissions": ["invoices.read","invoices.create"],
  "resource.path": "projects/prod/arn:res:tok_b58_xxx",
  "network.ip": "203.0.113.xxx",
  "pseudonymization_version": "1",
  "pseudonymization_key_id": "projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/evmap/cryptoKeys/evmap-key-2024"
}

Local audit trail (collector) - what to store (non-PII):
- event_id (UUID), transformation_applied (tokenize|mask|none), canonical_fields_transformed (list), key_id (KMS uri), transform_ts, collector_version.
- This trail must be encrypted and rotated. Retention default 30 days.

Re-identification workflow (emergency only):
1) Analyst opens an access request ticket (Jira: SEC-REID-xxxx) and selects the justification template.
2) Approval: >=2 approvers from security ops + legal required. Approvers must be distinct from requester.
3) Automation: on approval, a short-lived re-identification token is minted by KMS and a reid-service performs mapping, logs access, and returns original identifier to the requester via secure channel.
4) Reid events recorded to long-term audit with limited visibility (sec+legal).

Collector configuration snippet (YAML) - example:
policy_version: 1
fields:
  subject.id: { action: pseudonymize, deterministic: true, key_alias: evmap-key-2024 }
  subject.email: { action: mask, mask_strategy: local-part-asterisk }
  account.id: { action: pseudonymize, deterministic: true }
  network.ip: { action: mask, mask_strategy: last-octet }
  raw_payload: { action: omit }

Implementation guidance for engineers:
- Provide a shared pseudonymization lib (Go/Python/Java) that exposes deterministic_tokenize(value, field_name, key_alias) and opaque_mask(value, strategy). Collectors should call into this lib rather than rolling their own crypto.
- Key access must go through a single KMS client instance per process, with short-lived cached tokens.
- For high-throughput agents, prefer batching: collect N values, call HMAC in vectorized crypto backend.
- Integrate collector metrics: pseudonymize.latency_ms, pseudonymize.errors, pseudonymize.rate, policy.applied.count.

Migration plan (phases):
- Phase 0: experimental - ship lib to one agent type, enable pseudonymization for subject.email only. Test with SIEM dev cluster. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: rollout deterministic pseudonyms for subject.id and account.id in internal-only collectors. (4 weeks)
- Phase 2: enable for customer-facing collectors with feature flag and per-customer policy. (6 weeks)
- Phase 3: deprecate raw-id exports in default pipeline and update docs. (2 weeks)

Rollout checklist (short):
- [ ] Publish pseudonymization library and API docs
- [ ] KMS keys provisioned and ACLs defined
- [ ] Collector builds updated with policy parsing and tests
- [ ] SIEM dev cluster validated with mapped fields
- [ ] Run chaos tests: key-unavailable, high-latency KMS, collector restart scenarios
- [ ] Publish runbook for re-identification emergency flow

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we use key-per-tenant or single-key-with-tenant-context? (security favours per-tenant; ops complexity increases.)
- Migration of historical raw events in SIEM: provide migration tooling to backfill masked fields or rely on reid-only for new events?
- Legal: define retention maxima for local audit queue beyond default 30d.

References and links:
- Confluence: SEC-AUDIT-120 (audit schema canonicalization)
- Jira: SEC-5412 (collector pseudonymization epic)
- Slack: #sec-evidence (thread: pseudonymization-approach)

Notes to implementers / quick hacks: this doc contains some heuristics and suggestions. If you're in a rush, apply the following minimal safe changes: pseudonymize subject.id and account.id deterministically, mask emails by local-part, and purge raw_payload by default. Add a collector flag --pseudonymize=on and push metrics to the monitoring stack so we can iterate.

Author: Priya Nair (security operations)
Reviewed-by: Evans/Rodriguez (engineering), Maya Chen (privacy)
